hero.purpose: The home mission headline only, capped at 20-24ch, with photo chips woven into its words.

display.purpose: h1 and inner-route mastheads, capped at 20ch.

headline.purpose: h2 band headings at 22ch and the closing call to action at 20ch.

statement.purpose: The mission sentence at 34ch. The one place the display face sets a full sentence, and the only place weight 600 appears.

title.purpose: h3 — ledger titles, event titles, board names, pending headings; each overrides upward within its own component.

amount.purpose: Dollar figures in the ledger. The loudest non-heading element on the page.

numeral.purpose: The pillar index numerals, generated as 01, 02, 03.

lead.purpose: One sentence under a headline. 34ch beside a hero, 52ch under a masthead, 46ch as a section lede.

body.purpose: All reading copy, capped at 60ch by default and 54-58ch inside mission and event bodies.

small.purpose: Meta lines, notes, hints, bios, footer copy, and a quiet amount label when a figure is not a plain dollar value.

control.purpose: Buttons, nav links, and form labels (0.95rem in a field label).

label.purpose: Footer column headings, the cancelled flag, and the caption line inside the next-event card.

shadows.name: resting-lift
shadows.purpose: Barely there. Mosaic photos, event photos, board portraits, and the resting tomato button.

shadows.name: response-lift
shadows.purpose: Any button on hover, a hovered mosaic photo, the mobile nav panel, the masthead photograph, the resting photo chip, and the resting next-event card.

shadows.name: hero-lift
shadows.purpose: The wide hero photograph, and the hover state of the two elements that float over a photograph.

shadows.name: inset-hairline
shadows.purpose: How a flat surface gets an edge: pending panel, form disclaimer, success note, board initials placeholder, empty photo frame.

shadows.name: focus-glow
shadows.purpose: The only coloured glow in the system. Form field focus, paired with a full-ink border.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default exponential deceleration for reveals, lifts, and shadow transitions.

motion.name: ease-emph
motion.purpose: Emphasised deceleration for rotation and scale: photo chips, the next-event card, the logo seal.

motion.name: dur-1
motion.purpose: Colour-only changes (background, border, text), always linear.

motion.name: dur-2
motion.purpose: Button lift, nav underline, skip link, date box.

motion.name: dur-3
motion.purpose: Ledger row slide, photo hover, next-event straighten.

motion.name: reveal-offset
motion.purpose: The idle state of a revealable element; only exists inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

narrative.overview:
The organization's whole meaning is that neighbours bought the things kids play on — floor hockey goals for $500, a playground bucket seat for $515, dugouts for $15,430. The site is therefore a ledger: warm editorial type carrying the organization's own photographs, and a deep green field where years, objects, and dollar amounts are set as display type loud enough to be the proof.

The register is warm, bold, and civic rather than institutional. Everything sits on one of five grounds — warm paper, a warm tint, the deep green field, the tomato field, or the ink footer — and a section's identity comes from which ground it stands on, not from a container drawn around it. Type does the structural work: headings run oversized, mixed case, with the `wdth` axis narrowed as the size grows, while reading copy stays in Atkinson Hyperlegible at a generous 1.62 line height because families and older board members read this. Lists are separated by hairline rules rather than boxed into cards, and photographs are the only elements permitted to look lifted.

Density is low and deliberate: long vertical bands, wide measures capped in characters rather than pixels, and single-column reading at every width. The layout never fakes evidence — where content is a launch dependency (the board roster, the donation URL, the event calendar) a composed pending panel states the truth instead of filling the space with plausible fiction.
keyCharacteristics: A ledger, not a brochure: years, objects, and dollar amounts carry the argument.
Five tonal grounds (paper, tint, green field, tomato field, ink footer) instead of decorative containers.
Oversized Bricolage Grotesque headings, narrowed and tightly tracked; Atkinson Hyperlegible for everything read.
Amounts are always tabular display figures.
Every photograph is generously rounded (18–28px) and slightly tilted where it is small.
Near-flat: depth comes from ground changes, hairline rules, and photographic shadow only.
Pill controls, hairline fields, no card borders.
Motion is enhancement only; content is visible without JavaScript and without motion.

rules.name: The Gold-As-Marker Rule
rules.body: Gold marks, it never narrates. Its permitted roles are the highlighter stroke, the signpost tick on the green field, the amount figure on the green field, the focus glow, the selection wash, the hover underline, and the Donate fill on dark grounds. It is never a text colour on paper, never a resting surface in a paper band, and never a large flat area at full strength — the ambient washes sit at 24–30%.

rules.name: The Ground Decides the Accent Rule
rules.body: A section's ground chooses its accent. On paper and tint, amounts and index numerals are tomato and rules are 14% ink. On the green field, amounts are gold and rules are 22% field-ink. On the tomato field and the ink footer, Donate reverses to paper or gold so it stays the loudest thing present.

rules.name: The Tomato Is Action Rule
rules.body: Tomato means do something or here is the count: Donate, the numerals, the amounts on paper, the nav underline, the role line. It never sets body copy, and the one field it grounds carries at most 46ch of text.

rules.name: The Tabular Amount Rule
rules.body: Every dollar figure is a tabular display figure (Bricolage 700, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`). A value that is not a plain dollar amount drops to quiet Atkinson small instead, so an unverifiable figure never wears the display weight.

rules.name: The Narrow-When-Loud Rule
rules.body: The larger the type, the narrower the `wdth` axis and the tighter the tracking: 100% at control and label sizes, 94% at statement, 92% at `h1`–`h3`, 90% at amounts, 88% at hero and index numerals, with tracking moving from -0.01em to -0.05em across the same range.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Bricolage never sets reading copy and Atkinson never sets a heading. Measures are capped in characters, not pixels: 60ch body, 52–56ch notes and summaries, 46ch ledes, 34ch statements and hero leads, 20–24ch headings.

rules.name: The Band, Not the Box Rule
rules.body: Structure comes from full-bleed horizontal bands changing ground colour, each re-centring the same `84rem` column. Never nest a coloured container inside a band to fake a section.

rules.name: The Unequal Stagger Rule
rules.body: Repeating sequences are never a stack of equal rows. The three pillars indent 0/3/6% at 52rem and 0/6/12% at 72rem, the mosaic promotes its first and sixth cells to double-wide squares, and the mosaic photos alternate a -1.1° / +0.9° rotation.

rules.name: The Photograph Earns the Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to photographs, to elements floating over a photograph, and to hover or focus response. A flat surface that needs definition takes an inset 1px hairline, never a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is mixed from warm ink (`rgb(23 20 14 / …)`) at 6–38%. No grey, no black, no coloured glow — with the single exception of the focus glow on a form field, which is a 3px gold ring at 45%.

rules.name: The Rounded Photograph Rule
rules.body: Every photograph is rounded — 18px in rails and grids, 28px on wide panels and square portraits, interpolated on inline chips. A square-cornered image is a defect.

rules.name: The Pill Control Rule
rules.body: Anything you click is a pill (`999px`). Anything that holds content is gently rounded (10/18/28px). The two vocabularies never trade places.

rules.name: The Rules-Not-Cards Rule
rules.body: Every list of records — projects, events, places, footer links — is separated by 1px hairlines and nothing else. No borders, no fills, no boxes per item.

rules.name: The Motion-Is-Enhancement Rule
rules.body: Content is visible by default. Every animation lives inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, reveals fire once when an element crosses 92% of the viewport height, and a `<noscript>` rule forces every revealable element visible. Easing is exponential deceleration only (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` and `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`) across four durations (180/320/620/900ms). Nothing loops, nothing hijacks the scroll.

dos: Do stand each section on one of the five grounds (paper #fbf8f2, tint #f1ebdf, green field #0e4a2c, tomato field #c6371c, ink footer #17140e) and let the ground choose the accent — see The Ground Decides the Accent Rule.
Do set every dollar figure as a tabular Bricolage display figure, and drop non-plain amounts to quiet Atkinson small — see The Tabular Amount Rule.
Do narrow the `wdth` axis and tighten tracking as type gets larger (100% → 88%, -0.01em → -0.05em).
Do round every photograph: 18px in grids and rails, 28px on wide panels and square portraits.
Do separate records with 1px hairlines (14% ink on paper, 22% field-ink on the green field).
Do keep controls as pills and containers as 10/18/28px rounds.
Do cap measures in characters: 60ch body, 46ch ledes, 34ch statements, 20–24ch headings.
Do give launch-dependent content a composed pending panel (tint ground, 28px radius, inset hairline) that states the truth and offers a real next action.
Do wrap every animation in `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and keep the `<noscript>` visibility guarantee.
Do stagger repeating sequences so they read as unequal — indents, spans, alternating tilts.
donts: Don't use flat municipal colour bands.
Don't set timid, undersized type. The hero reaches 7.5rem and amounts reach 2.9rem for a reason.
Don't build a 50/50 split hero. The hero body is asymmetric (1.25fr / 0.75fr) with a full-width photograph beneath it.
Don't present three matching equal impact cards. The pillars are unequal typographic statements with index numerals.
Don't let metric tiles stand in for evidence. Named objects, years, and amounts are the evidence.
Don't reach for a generic card grid or the shadcn look.
Don't use glassmorphism, blobs, or gradient decoration beyond the two clipped gold ambient washes.
Don't scroll-jack, loop an animation, or gate content behind JavaScript.
Don't put gold on paper as a text colour or a resting surface — see The Gold-As-Marker Rule.
Don't draw a card border or nest a coloured container inside a band to fake a section.
Don't use a grey or black shadow; all shadows are warm ink at 6–38%.
Don't invent aggregate claims or filler content to make a layout look full.
